name: com.producthunt/mcp
title: Product Hunt
description: Discover apps, AI tools and MCP servers, compare alternatives, and manage your launches and ads.

tools.name: get_my_account
tools.description: Return the authenticated Product Hunt account identity.

tools.name: get_launch_context
tools.description: Read composer limits, account eligibility, midnight-Pacific date availability, the existing product a link belongs to, your matching draft, and bounded topic/category/maker/funding backer/shoutout product suggestions. With no product, the launch is a new product and needs no product question. Availability is a snapshot, not a reservation.

url.description: Product link to resolve: its existing product, your unsubmitted draft for this exact link, and a recent launch of it.

product_id.description: Numeric Product ID; resolves this product instead of url's.

launch_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD day in America/Los_Angeles to check for a launch at 00:00 Pacific; the result is in date.

topic.description: Topic name to search; returns topic IDs for topics.

category.description: Category name to search; returns category IDs for categories.

maker.description: Username or name to search; returns user IDs for makerIds.

funding_backer.description: Funding backer name to search; returns backer IDs for fundingBackers.

shoutout_product.description: Product name to search; returns product IDs for shoutouts productId.

tools.name: list_my_launches
tools.description: List launches you own or manage as hunter, maker, or active product team member, most recently changed first. status is draft (not submitted), unscheduled, scheduled, or live. Read one with get_launch and its launch_id. permitted_actions lists the tools and website editing that apply to each item; the write tools appear only when this connection can edit launches.

product_id.description: Numeric Product ID; only launches for this product.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; valid only with the same product_id, status and limit.

tools.name: get_launch
tools.description:
Read one launch you own or manage as its hunter, maker or product team member: its content, what still needs work, and what can still change.

In the result:
- status is draft, unscheduled, scheduled or live. Until its launch day starts only you and its makers can see it; once live, every change is public.
- assessment lists what still needs a change or a decision, the programs (contests, Hypership) open on its launch day, and investor questions with their prompt IDs.
  Resolution options are alternatives; suggestions are optional.
- editable_fields names the fields that can still change. You are a maker when makers lists you.
- hunter is who hunts a submitted launch; pending_hunter_invite is an invite to a new hunter, changed with update_launch hunterInvite.
- editable_section_urls opens a website panel (media, company_info, investor_questions) when the user wants to edit there; otherwise link url.

When discussing the launch, briefly mention relevant assessment suggestions without waiting to be asked, and keep blockers apart from optional improvements.
Suggest a next step, but ask before changing anything.

launch_id.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

tools.name: open_launch_editor
tools.description: Show the user a launch as its Product Hunt page, in an editor where they can change it themselves. Call it when the user wants to see their launch or edit it themselves, not to read it for yourself (use get_launch). Opening it changes nothing. The result is the launch as get_launch reads it. Edits the user saves there go through update_launch, so the launch's revision may change; read it again before your next update_launch.

launch_id.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

tools.name: get_launch_preview_view
tools.description: For the launch preview app only: the launch as the website composer renders it, with changes that are previewed but not applied yet.

launch_id.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

changes.description: Unapplied update_launch changes to render as proposed.

tools.name: start_launch
tools.description: Start a launch for a product link, or resume your existing unsubmitted launch for the same link and product choice without changing it (created: false). Omit product_choice for a new product; nothing needs confirming. Only when get_launch_context finds an existing product for the link, ask the user whether this launch belongs to it, then send product_choice "existing" with its product_id; a link that belongs to an existing product is refused as new. values uses the same fields as update_launch changes, except images, which are prepared for the returned launch_id. The launch starts as a private draft: starting it never submits, schedules or enrolls it. The result is the launch as get_launch reads it. If the outcome is unknown, retry the identical request with the same idempotency_key; a retry returns the original launch.

url.description: The product link, http or https, without spaces; not a Product Hunt link.

product_id.description: Numeric product ID from get_launch_context product.id; required with product_choice existing and refused otherwise.

tools.name: update_launch
tools.description:
Change a launch you own or manage, at any status. Change only fields in get_launch editable_fields.

- Draft: a draft is private, so every change, including added makers, applies directly (outcome applied), even when incomplete. It never submits, schedules or enrolls
  the launch.
- Submitted or live: public changes, moving the launch's day, and notifying added makers return outcome needs_confirmation and change nothing. Which edits are public
  cannot be predicted, since even a launch that is not live yet can change a public product page, so send changes without preview and let the server decide. On
  needs_confirmation, show the preview, reasons and side_effects, get explicit user approval, then resend with confirmation_token and without preview.

A token proves a preview was returned, not user approval: never send one the user did not approve.

Use preview true only when the user wants to inspect an edit before deciding whether to make it, never to check whether it needs confirmation. If they already
requested draft edits and want to see the submission first or say not to submit yet, save the edits, then call submit_launch without a token to preview the
complete submission.

On revision_conflict nothing changed: reread the launch, keep the user's requested changes, ask about competing edits, and send only those changes.

expected_revision.description: Revision from get_launch or the previous result.

idempotency_key.description: If the outcome is unknown, retry the identical request with this same key to avoid applying it twice.

confirmation_token.description: Valid for 15 minutes. After user approval, resend the same launch, revision and changes with this token, without preview. Bound to this account and connection; differences are confirmation_invalid. Empty means omitted.

preview.description: True changes nothing and returns needs_confirmation with a preview and token, even for private edits. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

tools.name: submit_launch
tools.description:
Submit a draft launch so it is scheduled for its launch day, or created unscheduled and not public when it has no launchDate.
It always takes two calls, and only the second one submits.

1. Call without confirmation_token. Nothing is submitted; the result is outcome needs_confirmation with preview.submit (the complete submission as Product Hunt
   would carry it out), side_effects (what it does and what becomes public), warnings and a confirmation_token valid for 15 minutes.
   validation_failed means something blocks submission; fix it with update_launch first.
2. Show the user the preview and side_effects and get their explicit confirmation. Then call again with confirmation_token: the launch is created and every side effect
   happens, such as adding makers, posting the first comment, publishing shoutouts, entering programs and notifying followers.

The token proves a preview was returned, not that the user approved it. If the launch, its launch day, permissions or assets changed since, nothing is submitted
(confirmation_invalid). A submitted launch's launch_id becomes its numeric ID.

launch_id.description: UUID launch_id of the draft to submit, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

idempotency_key.description: Retry key for this account and connection, bound to launch_id and confirmation_token. If the outcome is unknown, retry the identical request with the same key; a retry returns the launch, even after the token expires.

confirmation_token.description: confirmation_token from the needs_confirmation result; send it only after the user approved that preview. Empty means omitted.

preview.description: True only previews, as omitting confirmation_token does. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

tools.name: prepare_launch_asset
tools.description:
Stage a thumbnail or gallery image for a launch you own or manage. Staging changes neither the displayed images nor the launch revision:
once the asset is ready, attach it with update_launch thumbnailAssetId or ordered galleryAssetIds for the same launch_id.

Images are PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 10 MB, 10000 pixels per side and 40 megapixels. Send the bytes one of three ways:
1. source_url, when the image is already at a public URL.
2. For a local file, prefer the upload: call without source_url or content, then POST the file as multipart field file to upload.url on www.producthunt.com
   with upload.headers before upload.expires_at, for example: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <upload ticket>" -F file=@image.png <upload.url>
   The ticket covers only this asset; never send this connection's own token there.
3. content, only when you cannot reach www.producthunt.com.

launch_id.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

kind.description: thumbnail assets go in thumbnailAssetId, gallery assets in galleryAssetIds.

source_url.description: Public HTTP or HTTPS image URL the server downloads. Not with content.

content.description: Base64 image bytes from a tool such as base64, at most 3 MB decoded, without a data: prefix; line breaks are ignored. Not with source_url. Your client may allow less than 3 MB; if it rejects the call, send a smaller image.

idempotency_key.description: Names this asset for this account and connection; reuse it only with the same launch_id, kind and source_url. Retry with the same key to get the same asset, a fresh ticket, or another try at content after a failure; a ready asset accepts only its same bytes.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Send feedback about the Product Hunt MCP to the Product Hunt team. Call only when the user explicitly asks you or approves requests to do so. Encourage the user to leave feedback when a tool or upload fails, results are wrong or confusing, a capability is missing, or a step needs a workaround, unless they've previously declined. Never include secrets or personal details about anyone.

kind.description: broken: a tool failed or returned wrong data. confusing: a tool, its arguments, or its output were unclear. missing: no tool offers what the user needed. idea: a suggestion to improve an existing tool.

message.description: What the user wanted, what you tried (tool calls and arguments), what happened, and what would have helped.

tool.description: Name of the tool the feedback is about, if any.

impact.description: blocked: the task could not be finished. worked_around: finished another way. friction: finished, but harder than it should be.

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: List all available Product Hunt categories with their slugs. - When to use: When you need to find the right slug for search_products' category filter, or when the user asks what categories Product Hunt has, or wants to browse available topics. - Returns: All searchable categories organised by parent/child hierarchy with slugs. Use the slug values directly as search_products(category).

tools.name: get_product_profile
tools.description:
Get one product's details to decide whether it fits: what it does, pricing, rating, a summary of its reviews with
what users like and dislike, its MCP server endpoints when it has them, links, makers, company and funding.

Use it after a search, before recommending or connecting a product, and for "tell me about X", "is X any good"
or "who made X". product_name takes a name, a slug or the name of one of its launches; matched_by says which
matched, so check it is the product the user meant.

A maker is anyone credited on a launch, not necessarily a founder, with their Product Hunt profile, headline and
LinkedIn/X links when public. company has YC batch, founded date, team size and operating status. funding has
total raised, latest round and notable investors. series_a_band appears when the latest launch ranks in the top
bands of Product Hunt's Series A forecast.

product_name.description: Product name or slug to look up (e.g., "notion", "linear", "figma").

tools.name: find_investable_startups

query.description: A topic or audience to narrow the shortlist, as a short phrase such as "voice AI", "consumer social app" or "healthcare software". One topic per call. Matched by meaning against what each product does and who it is for; a launch whose name or tagline contains every word also matches.

category_slug.description: Filter by category slug. Use get_categories to discover valid slugs and pick the most specific matching one (e.g. "ai-dictation-apps" for dictation queries, not the broader parent).

launched_after.description: Earliest launch date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Set only when the user named a window; otherwise omit (default: 30 days before launched_before). launched_after and launched_before can be at most one year apart.

launched_before.description: Latest launch date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Set only when the user named a window; otherwise omit (default: today).

yc_only.description: Only startups Product Hunt has matched to a Y Combinator company. Set it only when the user asked for YC companies.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous response, unchanged, with the same other arguments. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: search_products

query.description: A product name or a short phrase for what it does. Constraints such as price, open source, YC or dates go in their own fields, not here.

category.description: Only products in this category: a slug from get_categories.

launched_within_days.description: Only products with a launch in the last N days (1 = today). Do not combine with launched_after or launched_before.

launched_after.description: Only products with a launch on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific time. For named periods.

launched_before.description: Only products with a launch on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific time. For named periods.

pricing.description: Only products with this pricing; any for no pricing filter.

open_source.description: true for open source products only; any for no filter.

yc.description: true for Y Combinator companies only; any for no filter.

platform.description: Only products available on this platform; any for no filter. From the app store links on the product. Mac, Windows and other platforms are not covered: put them in query.

has_mcp_server.description: true when the user wants a product their AI agent can connect to, such as an MCP server for a task: only products with an MCP server, each with its endpoints. any for no filter.

sort.description: Only without query: a query is ranked by relevance, except "alternatives to X". Leave out unless the user asks for an order; a date window alone does not need one. Default highest_rated. newest is the latest launch first; most_points ranks by the points of launches in the window.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous response, sent with the same other arguments. Paging covers at most 100 results.

intent.description: One sentence on the wider task and why you chose this tool, in general terms: no names, product or company names, argument values or secrets. Recorded only; it never changes results.

tools.name: get_product_leaderboard
tools.description:
Get Product Hunt's official leaderboard: the products that ranked for a day, in rank order, each
with its ranked launch and points. date is a day (YYYY-MM-DD); it also takes an ISO week
(YYYY-Www), a month (YYYY-MM) or a year (YYYY). Omit date for today. Days are Pacific time, and
today's leaderboard is still changing. To search or filter launches, use search_products.

date.description: A day (YYYY-MM-DD), ISO week (YYYY-Www), month (YYYY-MM) or year (YYYY), Pacific time. Omit for today.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous response, sent with the same date. Paging covers at most 100 products.

intent.description: One sentence on the wider task and why you chose this tool, in general terms: no names, product or company names, argument values or secrets. Recorded only; it never changes results.

tools.name: get_alternatives
tools.description:
Find alternatives to one Product Hunt product, most similar first: products that do the same job,
without the product itself. product takes a product's slug, name or Product Hunt URL; the
response names the product it matched, so check it is the one the user meant. For alternatives
with a price, platform or date constraint, or to search by need, use search_products.

product.description: Slug, name or Product Hunt URL of the product to find alternatives for, e.g. notion or cursor.

intent.description: One sentence on the wider task and why you chose this tool, in general terms: no names, product or company names, argument values or secrets. Recorded only; it never changes results.

tools.name: search_mcp_servers
tools.description:
Find MCP servers an AI agent can connect to for a task, from products on Product Hunt, best fit first.
Each result has the server's endpoints and what its makers say it does (mcp_server) and the launch that lists it.

Use it when the user asks which MCP server to use for something, especially alongside the tools they already use.
search_products with has_mcp_server also finds MCP servers and adds date and sort; use it to look up products in general.

Send query, tools_used, or both. Examples:
- "an MCP server for sending email" → {"query": "sending email"}
- "I use Cursor and Linear, which MCP servers help with sprint planning?" → {"query": "sprint planning", "tools_used": ["Cursor", "Linear"]}

query.description: The task or use case as a short phrase, such as "query Postgres" or "browser automation". Leave out the word MCP and constraints that have their own fields.

tools_used.description: Names of products the user already uses, such as ["Cursor", "Linear"]. They are left out of the results, and servers whose launches mention them rank higher and list them in works_with.

category.description: Only products in this category: a slug from get_categories.

pricing.description: Only products with this pricing; any for no pricing filter.

open_source.description: true for open source products only; any for no filter.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous response, sent with the same other arguments.

intent.description: One sentence on the wider task and why you chose this tool, in general terms: no names, product or company names, argument values or secrets. Recorded only; it never changes results.

tools.name: ads_get_context
tools.description: List ad accounts accessible through your current portal membership. Follow next_after_id even when a page is empty. Every account can manage drafts and campaigns; access is always advertiser. With none, offer ads_create_account.

tools.name: ads_list_campaigns
tools.description: List campaigns reachable through your current membership in an ad account. Like the advertiser portal, it leaves out campaigns that ended before the account's visible history begins (usually about 12 months ago). Use ads_get_campaign for authorized budget schedules, delivery status, and editable creative slots.

tools.name: ads_get_campaign
tools.description: Read an authorized campaign, a page of its permitted budgets, and its self-serve portal creative state (slots, associated launch selection, and variant controls) when your membership reaches the campaign's asset request. live means an active, unpaused budget with live placements; daily limits, targeting, and auctions still affect delivery, and draft budgets never serve. creative is null when no current portal asset request is reachable. Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage. Commercial terms and billing details are not exposed; delivery results are in ads_get_performance.

tools.name: ads_get_performance
tools.description:
Read delivery results for an ad account you can access: impressions, clicks, CTR, CPM and spend in USD as totals and per campaign, ad type and creative,
plus a daily series. Pass campaign_id for one campaign.

Figures come from the advertiser portal's report, refreshed about hourly, over the same history as ads_list_campaigns (usually campaigns active in about the last
12 months). Spend is delivered value (impressions at the booked CPM) capped at each booking's budget; it is not an invoice.
Totals, campaigns, ad types and creatives always cover the whole report; days, start_date, end_date and breakdown shape only the daily series.
A series over 500 rows, counting each day and each breakdown row, is refused: narrow the dates or pass campaign_id.

days.description: Days in the daily series, ending on end_date; 30 when no dates are passed. Use instead of start_date and end_date.

start_date.description: First day of the daily series, YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific time, inclusive. Defaults to the first reported day.

end_date.description: Last day of the daily series, YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific time, inclusive. Defaults to the last reported day.

breakdown.description: Split each day of the daily series by ad_type or by creative; creative rows carry the id of an entry in creatives. none returns day totals only.

tools.name: ads_get_draft
tools.description: Read your current unfinished ad composer draft, available placement options, and text and image field limits. Requires account-wide portal access. A null draft means no saved work. Budgets and minimums are in whole USD; these are draft choices, not a price quote or reservation. A managed account's draft (mode request) is a campaign request with no budgets or checkout, so its min_budget is 0. Billing stays in the browser and is omitted here. draft.variants lists additional creative variants, whose creative_changes carry their variant_key; draft.launch is the linked Product Hunt launch, set with ads_update_draft post_id from a list_my_launches launch_id. An attached image shows its image_id, or null when it was uploaded in the browser. Open portal_url, select the advertiser, and open its composer to continue. Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage.

tools.name: ads_create_account
tools.description: Set up a self-serve Product Hunt ad account for the signed-in user, when ads_get_context lists none. Give what they promote: post_id of a Product Hunt launch they make or are on the team of, or website_url. budget_band is their approximate total budget. Set agency (and client_name) when booking for a client. The account's confirmed Product Hunt email becomes the contact and can sign in to Ads Manager. Product Hunt's ads team sees the request. A returning self-serve buyer gets their existing account back. This creates no campaign, draft, or payment. Next, call ads_start_draft with the returned advertiser_id.

tools.name: ads_start_draft
tools.description: Start an empty ad composer draft or return your current unfinished draft without changing it. Requires account-wide portal access. Other members' drafts are never returned. This saves no campaign, payment, submission, or live creative. Use ads_update_draft to fill it in. Repeating this call resumes your current open draft. Add images with ads_prepare_image. Finish checkout in the browser; a managed account's draft (mode request) has no checkout and is sent to the ads team from the browser. Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage.

tools.name: ads_update_draft
tools.description:
Save only the changes the user requested to their unfinished ad composer draft. Requires account-wide portal access.
Omitted fields and content added in the browser stay saved.

This never submits, publishes, charges, or changes a live campaign. Checkout happens in the browser, where a request-mode draft is sent to the ads team instead.
Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage.

expected_revision.description: write_revision from the draft. On a conflict or an uncertain retry, read ads_get_draft and reconcile before saving again.

note.description: Cannot include discount codes; the buyer adds those in the browser.

days.description: Omit for a managed request-mode draft.

placements.description: Replaces the whole list. Budgets are whole USD draft values, not payment authorization; a request-mode draft uses budget 0.

post_id.description: Links a prepay draft to the numeric launch_id of a scheduled or live launch from list_my_launches that you make or are on the product team of; null unlinks it. It leaves start_date as is, so start on or after draft.launch.earliest_start_date.

variant_key.description: A variant_key from draft.variants for a per_variant field; omit for the primary creative and for shared fields. Add the variant with add_variant_kinds first.

creative_changes.description: Updates only the named fields: value_text for creative_fields, or image_id of a ready image from ads_prepare_image for image_fields. Applied after remove_variant_keys and add_variant_kinds.

add_variant_kinds.description: Adds one empty creative variant per entry, for kinds in draft.variant_kinds; the new keys appear in draft.variants.

remove_variant_keys.description: Removes these draft.variants variants and their values.

tools.name: ads_prepare_image
tools.description:
Prepare an image for an ad draft field (draft_id, kind and asset_kind) or for an existing campaign image slot (campaign_id and slot_id), checked against the
returned constraints. Preparing does not change the draft or campaign: once status is ready, attach it with ads_update_draft creative_changes image_id
(with a variant_key for a variant) or ads_update_campaign slot_changes image_id.

Send the bytes one of three ways:
1. source_url, when the image is already at a public URL.
2. For a local file, prefer the upload: call without source_url or content, then POST the file as multipart field file to upload.url on www.producthunt.com
   with upload.headers before upload.expires_at, for example: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <upload ticket>" -F file=@image.png <upload.url>
   The ticket covers only this image; never send this connection's own token there.
3. content, only when you cannot reach www.producthunt.com.

draft_id.description: The draft, with kind and asset_kind from its image_fields. Not with campaign_id.

campaign_id.description: The campaign, with slot_id from ads_get_campaign creative.slots. Not with draft_id.

source_url.description: Public HTTP or HTTPS image URL the server downloads. Not with content.

content.description: Base64 image bytes from a tool such as base64, at most 3 MB decoded, without a data: prefix; line breaks are ignored. Not with source_url. Your client may allow less than 3 MB; if it rejects the call, send a smaller image.

idempotency_key.description: Names this image for this account and connection; reuse it only with the same target and source_url. Retry with the same key to get the same image, a fresh ticket, or another try at content after a failure; a ready image accepts only its same bytes.

tools.name: ads_update_campaign
tools.description:
Edit an existing campaign's self-serve creative slots, associated Product Hunt launch, or creative variants. Requires editable portal access for the campaign.
Commercial terms (name, budgets, dates, placements, pause state) are not editable here.

- Edits apply directly (outcome applied) and stay staged until ads_submit_campaign submits them; call it when the user is ready to submit.
- Removing a live or submitted variant, or passing preview true, changes nothing and returns outcome needs_confirmation with preview, side_effects and a
  confirmation_token valid for 15 minutes. Show the user and resend the identical request with confirmation_token after they confirm.
- Feed and billboard placements with a change in review on an approved campaign have locked true: they cannot edit slots or add variants until review
  finishes. Sponsor copy stays editable.

expected_revision.description: creative.write_revision from ads_get_campaign. On a conflict, read ads_get_campaign again and reconcile before retrying.

slot_changes.description: value_text for text, URL and HTML slots; image_id of a ready ads_prepare_image image for image slots; or clear_image true to clear an unsubmitted, unapproved image slot.

revert_slot_ids.description: Slots with can_revert true, returned to their approved or last-submitted value.

post_id.description: Stages an associated Product Hunt launch you are a maker or team member of, or null clears it. Slot values do not change.

add_variant_ad_types.description: Adds a variant group for each ad type in creative.variant_ad_types, up to 10 per placement.

remove_variant_keys.description: Keys from creative.removable_variant_keys. Removing a live or submitted variant needs the user's confirmation.

confirmation_token.description: confirmation_token from the needs_confirmation result; send it only after the user approved that preview.

preview.description: True changes nothing and returns needs_confirmation with a preview. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

tools.name: ads_submit_campaign
tools.description:
Submit an existing campaign's staged creative slot and associated launch changes for review. Requires editable portal access for the campaign.
It always takes two calls, and only the second one submits.

1. Call without confirmation_token. Nothing is submitted; the result is outcome needs_confirmation with preview (the slot_changes and launch_change to send),
   side_effects, warnings for empty required slots, and a confirmation_token valid for 15 minutes.
2. Show the user the preview and side_effects and get their explicit confirmation. Then call again with confirmation_token and without preview.

A token proves a preview was returned, not user approval: never pass one the user did not confirm. If the campaign changed since the preview, nothing is submitted
(confirmation_invalid). On managed campaigns with live ads, eligible slot changes may go live immediately; self-serve campaigns, launch changes and newsletter
sponsor copy wait for review.

confirmation_token.description: confirmation_token from the needs_confirmation result; send it only after the user approved that preview. Empty means omitted.

preview.description: True only previews, as omitting confirmation_token does. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

tools.name: ads_prepare_checkout
tools.description: Check whether your self-serve ad draft is ready to pay for and quote what checkout will book. Requires account-wide portal access. Pass write_revision as expected_revision. Managed request drafts are rejected. This never charges, holds a card, accepts terms, or submits anything: fix blocking_errors with ads_update_draft (uploading images via ads_prepare_image first), then give the buyer checkout_url to review the terms and pay in the browser. Totals over the card limit use payment_method ach, paid by bank or invoice in the browser. Amounts are whole USD. Unset dates usually don't block: the quote uses the start and length the browser fills in and lists them in quote.defaulted.
